title: Five Italian volunteers repatriated after detention during West Bank olive harvest
dek: Italy's foreign ministry confirmed their return on 24 October after Thursday's detention amid tensions over access to farmland.
summary: Five Italian women detained by Israeli authorities in the occupied West Bank on 22 October were repatriated on Saturday 24 October, Italy's foreign ministry said. They had been accompanying Palestinian olive growers with international volunteers. The detention, repatriation and broader allegations concerning settler violence are separate matters that require precise attribution.
body: Italy's foreign ministry confirmed on Saturday 24 October that five Italian activists had returned after being detained by Israeli authorities on Thursday in the occupied West Bank. Reuters and ANSA linked their presence to international accompaniment initiatives for Palestinian farmers harvesting olives south of Hebron, an important seasonal agricultural activity.

Italian consular officials visited the five women at the Tel Aviv airport on Friday evening and reported that they appeared in good physical condition, according to the foreign ministry. The reports placed their earlier detention at Kiryat Arba police facilities. Repatriation resolves the immediate custody issue but does not itself constitute a finding about the detention's legality.

The olive harvest is economically important to Palestinian farming communities and has long been associated with disputes over land access and personal safety. Reuters cited Israeli rights organization Yesh Din as recording more than 330 incidents of settler violence connected to this year's harvest. That is the organization's monitoring count, not a court finding on every incident.

Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani sought explanations from Israeli officials over the arrests. The women's return does not settle questions about the protection of farmers, access to orchards or possible liability for particular acts. Any subsequent legal judgment or official investigation should be reported separately from the fact of the activists' repatriation.
facts: Italy's foreign ministry confirmed the return of the five women on 24 October 2026.
The activists were detained on 22 October while accompanying Palestinian farmers in the West Bank.
perspectives: Tajani criticized the detention and requested explanations from Israeli authorities.
Yesh Din has documented alleged settler violence during the ongoing olive-harvest season.
unknowns: Final legal findings concerning the women's detention and responsibility for related incidents have not been established.

questions.question: When did the five women held near Kiryat Arba return to Italy?
questions.answer: Italy's foreign ministry confirmed repatriation on Saturday 24 October, two days after their detention while accompanying Palestinian olive growers.

questions.question: Why does the olive-harvest season draw international volunteer monitors?
questions.answer: Harvesting requires access to farmland and, according to rights monitors cited by Reuters, some growers face attacks and restrictions; volunteers accompany farmers and observe conditions.

impactReason: The repatriation resolves an Italian consular incident while highlighting broader access and human-rights concerns in the occupied West Bank.
